name: Somalia
tagline: The longest coastline in mainland Africa
summary: Three thousand kilometres of Indian Ocean, the painted rock shelters at Laas Geel that are among the oldest in Africa, and the Cal Madow mountains — a country with real destinations and real constraints on reaching them.
when: The cool season, November to March. Take current advice seriously; Somaliland and Puntland are the practical routes.

entries.caption: Three Thousand Kilometres
entries.description: The longest coastline on mainland Africa, most of it empty white sand.
entries.subject: an empty white sand beach on the Somali Indian Ocean coast

entries.caption: Cal Madow
entries.description: A mountain range behind Bosaso with cloud forest on top and frankincense on the slopes.
entries.subject: the escarpment of the Cal Madow mountains above dry plains

entries.caption: Speke's Gazelle and the Sea
entries.description: Speke's gazelle and dibatag inland, and turtles, dugong and whale sharks offshore.
entries.subject: a Speke's gazelle on stony ground in the Somali interior

entries.caption: Not the Circuit
entries.description: There are no game lodges. The wildlife here is coastal, and the interior is for those who know it.
entries.subject: arid acacia scrub and open plain in the Somali interior

entries.caption: Shimbiris
entries.description: 2,460 metres in the Cal Madow, the highest point, with juniper and cycads near the top.
entries.subject: juniper and cycads on the high slopes of Shimbiris

entries.caption: Seasonal, and Sudden
entries.description: The Shabelle and Juba run south; everything else runs for a fortnight after the rains.
entries.subject: a seasonal river running full through dry country after rain

entries.caption: The Juba and the Shabelle
entries.description: Two rivers off the Ethiopian highlands that make the only irrigated farmland in the country.
entries.subject: irrigated banana plantations along the Juba river

entries.caption: Berbera and Beyond
entries.description: Berbera's beaches on the Gulf of Aden, and a reef wall a short swim from the sand.
entries.subject: the beach and clear water at Berbera on the Gulf of Aden

entries.caption: Frankincense Country
entries.description: Boswellia trees on the Cal Madow slopes, tapped as they have been for four thousand years.
entries.subject: a tapped frankincense tree with resin beading on the bark

entries.caption: Diving Berbera
entries.description: Unfished reefs in the Gulf of Aden, and almost no one to share them with.
entries.subject: a diver over an unfished coral reef in the Gulf of Aden

entries.caption: Poetry as the National Art
entries.description: Somalis are called a nation of poets, and the reputation is deserved and enforced.
entries.subject: men listening to a poet reciting at an evening gathering

entries.caption: Nomad and Pastoralist
entries.description: Camel herding is the oldest way of life here and still a large part of the economy.
entries.subject: a Somali herder with camels on open thornbush country

entries.caption: Camel Milk and Bariis
entries.description: Camel milk, bariis iskukaris spiced with cumin and cardamom, and Somali tea with ginger.
entries.subject: a plate of bariis iskukaris with goat and banana

entries.caption: Weddings and Buraanbur
entries.description: Buraanbur — women's poetry with drumming and dance — carries the celebration.
entries.subject: women performing buraanbur poetry and dance at a wedding

entries.caption: Weaving and Woodcarving
entries.description: Aqal nomadic house frames, carved wooden headrests, and woven mats from the north.
entries.subject: the woven frame and mats of a Somali aqal nomadic house

entries.caption: Laas Geel
entries.description: Rock shelters near Hargeisa painted with cattle and people, five thousand years old and unfaded.
entries.subject: painted cattle and human figures on the rock shelters at Laas Geel

entries.caption: Ports of the Indian Ocean
entries.description: Mogadishu, Merca and Barawa were trading cities when Europe had none on this ocean.
entries.subject: the coral-stone ruins of an old trading house at Merca

entries.caption: Mogadishu and Hargeisa
entries.description: A white Indian Ocean capital rebuilding, and a highland city that has been quiet for thirty years.
entries.subject: the seafront and white buildings of Mogadishu

entries.caption: Coral Stone and Carved Doors
entries.description: Swahili coral-rag architecture along the southern coast, with heavy carved doors.
entries.subject: a carved wooden door in a coral-stone wall on the Somali coast

entries.caption: The Camel Market
entries.description: Hargeisa's livestock market on a weekday morning, and the money that moves through it.
entries.subject: traders and camels at the Hargeisa livestock market

entries.caption: Beaches, and Care
entries.description: Lido beach in Mogadishu fills at the weekend. Go with local advice, always.
entries.subject: families on Lido beach in Mogadishu at the weekend

entries.caption: Walking the Cal Madow
entries.description: Cool forest, cycads and views to the Gulf of Aden, from Erigavo.
entries.subject: a walking path through juniper forest in the Cal Madow

entries.caption: Beginning to Exist
entries.description: New hotels in Hargeisa and Mogadishu, mostly for business travellers, some of them good.
entries.subject: a rooftop terrace restaurant overlooking Hargeisa

entries.caption: Frankincense and the Land
entries.description: Boswellia grows on bare limestone where nothing else will, and it holds the slope together.
entries.subject: frankincense trees growing from bare limestone on a steep slope

entries.caption: Ochre on Rock
entries.description: Laas Geel in the morning, when the shelters are lit and the cattle look painted yesterday.
entries.subject: morning light on the painted rock shelter interior at Laas Geel

entries.caption: Berbera's Ottoman Quarter
entries.description: A decaying Ottoman and colonial old town by the harbour, being slowly repaired.
entries.subject: arched Ottoman-era buildings in the old town of Berbera

entries.caption: Why Somalia
entries.description: Rock art older than the pyramids, an unfished ocean, and a poetry tradition still practised daily.
entries.subject: a lone figure on an empty Somali beach at sunrise
